{"title":"Cohort Overview","sql":"
SELECT 
  COUNT(*) as total_patients,
  COUNT(DISTINCT `care_site_id`) as num_sites,
  AVG(`age_at_index`) as avg_age,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `sex` = 'Male' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) as pct_male,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `is_advanced` = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) as pct_advanced,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `event_flag` = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) as pct_deceased,
  AVG(`total_cost_of_care`) as avg_total_cost,
  AVG(`n_treatment_lines`) as avg_treatment_lines,
  AVG(`os_months_observed`) as avg_os_months
FROM `af_vault_genie_demo`.`nsclc_rwe_scoped`.`gold_patient_master_scoped`
"}

output.name: execute_sql
output.arguments:
{"title":"Survival by Primary Driver Mutation","sql":"
SELECT 
  `primary_driver`,
  COUNT(*) as patient_count,
  AVG(`os_months_observed`) as avg_os_months,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY `os_months_observed`) as median_os_months,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `event_flag` = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as deceased_count,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY CASE WHEN `event_flag` = 1 THEN `os_months_observed` END) as median_os_deceased
FROM `af_vault_genie_demo`.`nsclc_rwe_scoped`.`gold_patient_master_scoped`
WHERE `primary_driver` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `primary_driver`
ORDER BY median_os_months DESC
"}

content.text:
## Most Interesting Trends in Advanced NSCLC Patient Data

This cohort of **13 advanced-stage NSCLC patients** at your accessible sites reveals several striking patterns in treatment costs, survival outcomes, and the impact of clinical characteristics.

### 1. Dramatic Cost Disparity by Biomarker Status

**Patients with actionable driver mutations face 2-3x higher treatment costs**, driven overwhelmingly by pharmacy expenses.\[[1](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_015brazktntrfp88sptrgbv8)\]

- **ALK-positive**: $432K average total cost (76% pharmacy)
- **EGFR-positive**: $300K average total cost (76% pharmacy)
- **No actionable driver**: $152K average total cost (52% pharmacy)
- **KRAS**: $145K average total cost (47% pharmacy)

The cost difference is almost entirely attributable to targeted TKI therapy costs. Patients with ALK or EGFR mutations receive expensive targeted therapies that drive pharmacy costs to over $200K-$328K per patient, while those without actionable drivers rely more on chemotherapy and immunotherapy combinations with more balanced pharmacy/medical cost splits.\[[1](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_015brazktntrfp88sptrgbv8)\]

### 2. ECOG Performance Status Shows Non-Linear Relationship with Cost

**Worse performance status doesn't always mean higher costs**—ECOG 2 patients have the highest average costs ($287K) despite shorter survival.\[[2](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_018kvwskvckzlzvrws7uyvih)\]

- **ECOG 0**: 13.4 months median survival, $151K cost
- **ECOG 1**: 13.5 months median survival, $182K cost  
- **ECOG 2**: 8.7 months median survival, $287K cost (highest)
- **ECOG 3**: 6.1 months median survival, $145K cost

This suggests ECOG 2 patients may receive more aggressive interventions despite poor prognosis, while ECOG 3 patients may transition more quickly to palliative care. The mortality rate also climbs sharply: 60% for ECOG 0 to 100% for ECOG 2-3.\[[2](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_018kvwskvckzlzvrws7uyvih)\]

### 3. Targeted TKI Therapy: Highest Cost, Best Survival

**First-line treatment class reveals a clear cost-effectiveness trade-off**.\[[3](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_019axiqrq8hdkgg4mm785gis)\]

- **Targeted TKI**: $366K average cost, 14.1 months median survival (2 patients)
- **Chemo-IO**: $151K average cost, 9.4 months median survival (8 patients, most common)
- **IO monotherapy**: $148K average cost, 13.5 months median survival (3 patients)

Targeted TKI therapy costs 2.4x more than chemo-IO but delivers 50% longer median survival (14.1 vs 9.4 months). Interestingly, IO monotherapy achieves comparable survival to targeted therapy (13.5 months) at less than half the cost, though this may reflect patient selection—IO monotherapy patients also received more subsequent treatment lines (1.67 vs 1.0 for TKI patients).\[[3](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_019axiqrq8hdkgg4mm785gis)\]

### 4. Limited Treatment Intensification

**Most patients receive only 1-2 lines of therapy**, with counterintuitive cost patterns.\[[4](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_01wudzb31zyv8km1epo4iwwg)\]

- **1 line**: 9 patients, $197K average cost, 10.7 months median survival
- **2 lines**: 4 patients, $152K average cost, 11.5 months median survival

Patients receiving only one line of therapy actually have higher average costs ($197K vs $152K), likely because this group includes the high-cost targeted TKI patients who may have longer response durations on first-line therapy. The similar survival outcomes (10.7 vs 11.5 months) suggest that second-line therapy provides modest incremental benefit in this cohort.\[[4](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_01wudzb31zyv8km1epo4iwwg)\]

### 5. PD-L1 Expression Shows Unexpected Pattern

**Lower PD-L1 expression correlates with slightly better outcomes**, contrary to typical expectations.\[[5](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_01ptbpgd5t3ieny7klb4ni8s)\]

- **<1% PD-L1**: 13.4 months median survival, $168K cost (9 patients)
- **1-49% PD-L1**: 8.7 months median survival, $218K cost (4 patients)
- **≥50% PD-L1**: No patients in this cohort

The absence of high PD-L1 expressors (≥50%) is notable, as this group typically has the best immunotherapy response. The better outcomes in the <1% group may reflect the inclusion of patients with actionable mutations who received targeted therapy rather than immunotherapy.\[[5](https://adb-7405608383447105.5.azuredatabricks.net/genie/rooms/01f1c1bc36b518d7b7a59b21c1bd3b92/chats/01f1c288ca401ec287b4b56764e9547d?o=7405608383447105&gra_focus=toolu_bdrk_01ptbpgd5t3ieny7klb4ni8s)\]

### Key Takeaway

The data reveals a **fundamental tension between cost and survival**: targeted therapies for actionable mutations deliver the longest survival but at 2-3x the cost of standard chemo-immunotherapy. Performance status remains a critical prognostic factor, with ECOG 2-3 patients showing 100% mortality despite substantial treatment costs. The cohort's overall median survival of 12.1 months and 77% mortality rate underscore the continued challenge of advanced NSCLC management.[6]
